items.name: First screen
items.reason: Headline, the recommendation slot and c1 together say what to do (fix before relying on solo), why (clarity-case correctness 60% against a 90% bar, interval 37.8% to 78.7% wholly below), and the main risk (the lede: an uncalibrated judge, 0 calibration ratings). The flag adds that the bars warn and never gate. The accuracy pass is labelled as not settled.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 (clarity miss), c2 (accuracy passes on its point estimate only), c3 (clarity score lower, no line) follow from one another and match the decision slots. The one large tension, 95% correct in the accuracy run against 60% in the clarity run, is named in the judge_temperature caveat and next step 3 instead of being left unaddressed.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The recommendation says 'more cases will not change that, a change to the model or its prompt will'. The first half holds (the interval tops out at 78.7%). The second half promises a remedy the evidence does not support: the lede and the judge_temperature caveat both say the miss may be the judge's or the run setup's. c3 says the clarity score is 'lower' (3.6 against 4.2) without its uncertainty. The standard errors are 0.21 and 0.22, so the gap is about 1.9 combined SE, on a score with no stated scale. Neither c3 table prints the SE.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Cost (flat $2.00 per 1,000 replies, one arm), decision_sensitivity (bars never gate) and pass rate as its own measure are rightly omitted. Leaving out the campaign-wide scoreboard and the criterion-level figures is justified and checked: criteria.clarity/bar/answer.correct.solo.value reads 95%, the accuracy figure, while the clarity aspect's own bar reads 60%, and settle_cases sizes the clarity bar on that 95% too. One weak point: the failure examples are cut as showing 'nothing', but their case ids do carry information (clarity failures at tc-12, tc-13, tc-14; the one accuracy failure is tc-19 twice). That information bears on next step 3. See findings.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The uncalibrated judge, the absence of any declared line, and the unreported judge temperature each carry a material_if clause. Whether the two aspects ran the same cases is carried into next step 3, which says what each answer would point to. The apparatus caveats (reach: method) land once in Method, which says whether they varied between the two runs cannot be established. The confounds are carried, but the recommendation does not yet reflect them (item 3).

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an experiment or declaration and what it settles. Step 5 ('Run the accuracy cases to about 314 trials') would not settle what it claims. settle_cases sizes 314 in trials, using a standard error that treats trials as independent (spread counts = trials, n = 40). But Method says intervals are over cases, and the only accuracy failure is one case (tc-19) failing on both repeats. More repeats of the same 20 cases would not narrow a case-level interval; the step needs new cases. Order matters too: step 3 (confirm the two aspects ran the same cases) is cheap and could redirect steps 1 and 2, yet it sits third. Step 1 already assumes the fix is 'in the model's prompt'.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The counterfactual holds for every claim. But neither c1 block alone shows the claim 'whole interval sits below the bar'. c1/1 is a dot_interval that prints the value (60%) and the 90% floor with no interval. c1/2 prints the interval (0.3866 to 0.7812) on a 0 to 1 scale with no bar line. That interval also differs from the text's 37.8% to 78.7%. c2 has the same split. c3 compares one figure across aspects in two separate tables, which repeat answer.correct and show no SE. One table with both aspects and the SE would be clearer.

findings.finding: The recommendation slot asserts 'a change to the model or its prompt will' change the clarity-case result. The report's own lede and its judge_temperature caveat say the miss may be the judge's or the run setup's. Keep 'more cases will not change that' (the interval tops out at 78.7%, under 90%). Replace the remedy clause with what is known: solo is not ready on these cases, and whether the cause is the model or the judge is open until next steps 2 and 3.

The frozen failures carry case ids that bear on the report's central open question. Clarity failed tc-12, tc-13 and tc-14 (repeat 1). Accuracy's only failures are tc-19 on both repeats, so if the ids name the same cases, tc-12 to tc-14 passed every accuracy trial. Both aspects ran 20 cases with 2 repeats, the trial numbering suggests ids tc-00 to tc-19 in each, and the clarity failures (16 of 40) fit exactly 8 cases failing on every repeat. Next step 3 should state what the ids already suggest and move ahead of step 1, since it decides whether step 1 (fix the prompt) or step 2 (calibrate the judge) comes first. The omitted entry's 'a card would show nothing' undersells the examples.

Next step 5 and the watch slot cite about 314 trials (settle.criteria.accuracy/bar/answer.correct.solo.overall.cases_needed_two_sided_80). That count assumes trials are independent (n = 40 trials), but intervals are over cases and the accuracy failures sit in one case. 'Run the accuracy cases to about 314 trials' reads as more repeats of the same 20 cases, which would not settle the bar. Say that the extra trials must come from new cases, or flag the sizing as a lower bound.

Neither block shows the interval against the bar. c1/1 has the bar and no interval, and c1/2 has the interval and no bar, on a 0 to 1 scale while the text uses percent. c2 has the same split. Use one block that draws the bar-reading interval with the 90% bar as its reference line, in percent.

'Lower' rests on 3.6 against 4.2 with standard errors of 0.21 and 0.22 (about 1.9 combined SE) on an unscaled score, and neither table prints the SE. Show both aspects in one table with the SE, and soften to 'somewhat lower, on a score with no stated scale', or say the gap is near the noise.

invariant_concerns: Invariant 1: the omitted and method prose carry counts typed rather than read through a figure key: 'five frozen failed trials: one accuracy case twice, three clarity cases', 'the eight apparatus:world:* settings', 'eight world settings'.

Invariant 5: the omitted list names internal ids and tool names (options_dominance, count.failing, settle_cases, decision_sensitivity, apparatus:grader_version, apparatus:world:*). If the omitted section renders above the appendix, these breach the no-internal-id rule.
Method's 'Bars' entry cites criteria.accuracy/bar/answer.correct.threshold for both aspects. It reads 90%, which happens to equal the clarity threshold, but the clarity bar should cite its own key.
